newsitem.title: USA: AT&T sets Internet commerce service.
newsitem.headline: AT&T sets Internet commerce service.

text.p: AT&T Corp. Tuesday announced a service that it said would make doing business on the Internet as easy as dialing an 800 toll-free telephone number.

The nation's biggest long-distance phone company said it would offer a service that would allow businesses to build and maintain sites on the popular World Wide Web part of the Internet, as well as ways to attract customers to the site.

It also said it would guarantee credit card transaction security for people who shop on the Web, which has become a major concern of businesses and consumers trying to buy or sell via the computer network.
"AT&T revolutionised business with the invention of 800- toll-free service, and we intend to do no less for Web-based commerce," Chairman Robert Allen said in a statement.

AT&T said its offer was aimed at both consumers and merchants. It comes as many companies, concerned about security and other marketing difficulties, have said they will be content for now to view the Internet and the Web as marketing, rather than sales tools.
AT&T said it was hoping to change that view.
Allen said the company's new service would attract customers and "turn (Web) browsers into buyers."

Under its programme, AT&T said it would guarantee secure Internet transactions for Web shoppers who join the company's free Secure Buyer's programme and charge their Internet purchases to their AT&T Universal credit cards.
The company said that regardless of which Internet access provider consumers use, Web shoppers will not have to pay for purchases by unauthorised users.
AT&T itself offers Internet access through its Worldnet service.

AT&T also said merchants buying its Secure Buy service would not miss an order. It said it would refund the amount of a sale, up to the monthly Secure Buy service fee of $395 to $595 a month, if an order does not reach a merchant.
In addition, it said it would guarantee that customers using its service would never have their Web sites give the message "server not available," which is similar to a busy signal on the Web.
AT&T said it was also offering a series of services to stimulate Internet commerce.
AT&T's stock slipped 12.5 cents to $39.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
